lysC.Rationale: Overexpress a feedback-resistant mutant (e.g., lysC^T311I) to relieve allosteric inhibition by L-lysine and L-threonine, removing the primary bottleneck at the entry of the aspartate-derived lysine pathway.

dapA.Rationale: Dihydrodipicolinate synthase catalyzes the first committed step toward L-lysine/DAP; strengthening this branch-point enzyme increases carbon flux from aspartate semialdehyde toward lysine biosynthesis.

hom.Rationale: Downregulating homoserine dehydrogenase reduces drain of aspartate semialdehyde toward threonine/methionine, and lowers intracellular threonine pools, which synergistically weakens feedback inhibition on aspartate kinase.

thrB.Rationale: Partial attenuation of thrB prevents threonine over-accumulation and avoids back-conversion/repressive effects on the aspartate kinase reaction, improving net lysine flux.

pyc.Rationale: Overexpressing pyruvate carboxylase increases anaplerotic replenishment of oxaloacetate from pyruvate, supplying the carbon skeleton needed to support high-level lysine biosynthesis under aerobic glucose metabolism.

pck.Rationale: Reducing PEP carboxykinase activity prevents decarboxylation of oxaloacetate back to PEP during gluconeogenesis, conserving carbon and energy (ATP) and increasing oxaloacetate availability for the aspartate/lysine pathway.
